import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
coffee_sales = pd.read_csv('data/coffee_sales.csv')

# Create a new column for total sales by product
total_sales = coffee_sales.groupby('product')['total'].sum().reset_index()

# Set the style
sns.set(style="whitegrid")

# Create the bar plot
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
sns.barplot(data=total_sales, x='product', y='total', palette='viridis')

# Add labels and title
plt.xlabel('Product', fontsize=14)
plt.ylabel('Total Sales ($)', fontsize=14)
plt.title('Total Sales by Coffee Product', fontsize=16)
plt.xticks(rotation=45)
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
coffee_sales = pd.read_csv('data/coffee_sales.csv')

# Create a new column for total sales by product
total_sales = coffee_sales.groupby('product')['total'].sum().reset_index()

# Set the style
sns.set(style="whitegrid")

# Create the bar plot
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
sns.barplot(data=total_sales, x='product', y='total', palette='viridis')

# Add labels and title
plt.xlabel('Product', fontsize=14)
plt.ylabel('Total Sales ($)', fontsize=14)
plt.title('Total Sales by Coffee Product', fontsize=16)
plt.xticks(rotation=45)
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
